Re-reviewed the #3158 DelegationResultDelivery paragraph against 0528b693a3. 'An interrupt that names a turn suppresses only that turn, whether or not the log shows it yet, and it is suppressed even if it completed normally' matches the interrupt route passing the request's turnId to DelegationResultDelivery.beginCancel, which records `turnId ?? open ?? (coordinatorBusy ? undefined : null)` as a named (from_unlogged = 0) suppression that spend cancels whatever the outcome, mirroring CooperativeStop.applyPendingTurnInterrupt holding a named stop for that turn only. 'A turn that runs after a restart never takes one made before it' matches bindUnlogged's since-open epoch (created_at >= openedAt) used by bindUnloggedSuppressions (an open turn) and by record for a transition recorded as it lands; a late transition keeps the before-open epoch, so 'A transition found after a restart never takes a suppression made since' is unchanged. The no-active-turn undo sentence still holds: a named turn that is not the running one gets no-active-turn and settleCancellation refuses the cancel. orchestration.ts changed only in the delegated-task interrupt route, which now passes the request's existing optional turnId to DelegationResultDelivery.beginCancel (and names the validated body type); no route path, request schema, scope or authority check, or response field changed.
